title: [v0.4.26] Release: app wizard and capability editing
author: mcpdev80
body:
## CI foundation dependency correction — 2026-10-15

See #888/#893/#896 for the corrected order: #892 → #893 interface → #896 isolation → #893 final qualification → #895 protection. #896 may start from the agreed interface in PR #930 before #893 is complete. The product foundation acceptance requirements below remain unchanged; partial CI is not product-start clearance.

## Ausführbare Produkt-Tasks und Parallelität

Die Produktarbeit ist in **14 eigene Task-Issues** geschnitten; jeweils ein Ergebnis und eine eigene kleine PR gegen develop. #888/#890–#901 bleibt der separate Workflow-/CI-Auftrag. #752 ist ein unabhängiger zusätzlicher Pilot-Bug, kein versteckter Wizard-Task.

| Task | Ergebnis / Lane | Voraussetzung |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #910 | Wizard: gemeinsamen schreibfreien Bearbeitungszustand bereitstellen | qualifizierte PR-/Review-/Runner-Basis |
| #911 | App bearbeiten: vorhandene Auswahl vollständig laden | #910 |
| #912 | Wizard: kompakte bedarfsorientierte Auswahl anzeigen | #910 |
| #913 | Wizard: kompatible Provider optional in derselben Ansicht wählen | #910, #912 |
| #914 | Vorschau: tatsächlichen Footprint kompakt darstellen | #910 |
| #915 | Vorschau: Provider-Konsequenzen und Teilergebnisse verständlich zeigen | #910 |
| #916 | Wizard: Zurück, Abbruch und EOF ohne Nebenwirkungen behandeln | #912, #913, #914, #915 |
| #917 | App neu: kompakten Wizard an bestehenden Lifecycle anbinden | #916 |
| #918 | App bearbeiten: bestätigte Änderungen sicher anwenden | #911, #916 |
| #919 | Footprint: CLI und JSON aus derselben Projektion bedienen | #910, #914 |
| #920 | Maschinenadapter: Capability-Änderungen und Footprint gemeinsam nutzen | #910, #911, #919 |
| #921 | CLI und MCP: neue Oberflächen konsistent registrieren | #917, #918, #919, #920 |
| #922 | Doku: New/Edit und Providerwahl für Entwickler knapp erklären | #921 |
| #923 | Abnahme: New/Edit-Journey und Ökosystem-Verbrauch nachweisen | #921, #922 |

**Reihenfolge ohne gemeinsame Entwicklungsbranch:**

1. PR-/Review-/Runner-Basis #890–#893, #895/#896 und Produkt-Schnittstelle #910 qualifizieren. Eigene kleine Vorab-PRs; keine neue Resolver- oder State-Architektur.
2. Danach **#911, #912, #914 und #915 parallel**, mit unterschiedlichen Dateien. #913 nach #912; #919 nach #914. Der unabhängige Pilot #752 kann in eigener Lane laufen.
3. #916 verbindet erst die fertigen UI-Komponenten. Danach **#917 (New) und #918 (Edit) parallel**; #920 (Maschinenadapter) kann nach seinen ausgewiesenen Leseschnittstellen unabhängig folgen.
4. **#921 ist alleiniger Integrationstask für Commandbaum, Help, Machine/MCP-Registry, Discovery-/Coverage-Goldens und generierte Referenzen.** Vorgänger liefern kompilierende Handler/Adapter, ändern diese gemeinsamen Dateien nicht parallel.
5. #922 öffentliche EN/DE-Anleitung nach stabiler Oberfläche. #923 liefert die gezielte echte Produkt-/Consumer-Abnahme; Candidate/Evidence/GC aus #897–#900 müssen davor fertig sein. #901 besitzt den Kosten-/Parallelitätsvergleich.

**Dateikonflikte:** In jedem Task sind Scope und Dateigrenzen benannt. Ein Owner pro übernommenem Task, eigener Checkout/Branch, keine dauerhaften Dateisperren. Falls zwei Aufgaben doch dieselbe Schnittstelle ändern müssen: kleinen gemeinsamen Vorab-PR zuerst integrieren oder die betroffenen Schritte explizit sequenzieren; fremde Arbeit nicht überschreiben. Relevante Tests am tatsächlichen Integrationsstand erneut planen, kein automatischer Full-E2E für jeden PR.

**Hierarchie-Status:** Parent und Dependencies stehen in jedem Issue sowie obiger Tabelle als Text. Native GitHub-Unterissues/blocked-by-Beziehungen sind mit dem Connector nicht setzbar und müssen noch nachgetragen werden. Die Planung ist damit geschnitten; Regeln, CI und Reviews sind noch technisch umzusetzen.

---

## Zwei begrenzte Arbeitsbereiche in v0.4.26

1. **Produkt:** kompakter Create/Edit-Wizard sowie CLI/JSON/MCP-Footprint und Entwicklerdoku (dieses Issue).
2. **Arbeitsweise:** #888 — kleine Task-PRs, konservative Testauswahl, verständliche CI und sichere Release-Kandidaten.

Umstellung erst nach qualifiziertem v0.4.25-Abschluss. Eigene kleine PRs gegen develop; kein gemeinsamer Entwicklungsbranch und keine feste Zwei-Session-Zahl. Nach qualifizierter konservativer PR-CI-/Review-Basis dürfen Produkt- und Workflow-Aufgaben parallel laufen. Ein perfekter Impact-Analyzer oder feinere Fingerprints sind keine Voraussetzung. Sichere Candidate-/Evidence-/Promotion-Abnahme bleibt vor dem Release Pflicht. v0.4.25/#872/#881 bleibt unverändert.

## Binding scope correction (2026-10-11)

#872 is the authoritative corrected foundation: BaseHarbor-owned IDs, automatic/explicit provider realization, no fixed Core bundle, and complete ownership-safe add/remove/re-add convergence. These are v0.4.25 acceptance requirements, not deferred v0.4.26 work. This issue adds the developer interaction surface only. It must not reintroduce manual IDs, a mandatory bundle, legacy migration or a second resolver.

One compact wizard captures capabilities and optional provider preferences using existing owners. Automatic is default; no forced extra provider question/file. Editing hydrates the existing choices, previews actual service changes and retained data, and invokes the accepted v0.4.25 lifecycle. “No” retains choices; cancel/EOF never writes.

## Goal
Make v0.4.25 Capability-first semantics easy to create and change without new domain or provider contracts.

## Product workstream — Human wizard/TUI
- `baha app new` compact single-screen multi-select SQL, cache, managed secrets, identity/login, public HTTPS; zero selection valid, detected preselection visible and editable; other capabilities progressively disclosed.
- Short resolved preview (required services, new/reused containers, incremental memory with measured/estimated/unknown label); Yes proceeds normal lifecycle, No returns to same retained selections indefinitely, Cancel does not mutate.
- `baha app edit` with exact intent diff, effects and explicit confirmation; non-TTY/EOF/`--no-input` no silent defaults/mutation. Manual canonical/shorthand edit supported by same reconcile.
- No dead ends and compact contextual help. Own TUI, human wizard/command presentation.

## Product workstream — Surfaces and developer docs
- `baha app footprint show`, plan/CLI/JSON/MCP share v0.4.25 resolver; typed machine confirmation/denial and effective evidence.
- Console consumes same domain operations where applicable, no second resolver; keep full Console management journeys in v0.4.28.
- EN/DE documentation, discovery and automated CLI/JSON/MCP parity; own machine/UI adapters and public docs, not TUI or resolver internals.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Checklists, back-loop and preview verified with real and unknown capacity, reuse and zero-core.
- [ ] Changes at any point show diffs, are idempotent and preserve data/shared services.
- [ ] Noninteractive and EOF safety, no password/credential leakage, CLI/JSON/MCP parity.
- [ ] Independent developer path and exact-SHA runtime evidence.
- [ ] No new domain semantic without explicit v0.4.25 contract review.

Depends on fully accepted v0.4.25/#872; final acceptance #174. Small task branches/PRs follow #888; qualify the actual integration/candidate SHA.

## Binding UX clarification — provider choice in the SAME wizard, without requiring app.id (2026-10-10)

- Developer enters a minimal app contract (`version: 1`, `app.name`, `app.environment`); **never prompt for, accept or request a developer-supplied app UUID** in YAML, flags or other input. System-generated canonical IDs remain internal state/output. ID lifecycle/owner is defined in #872 and reused here.
- Single-screen capability multi-select stays the default. E.g. SQL, cache, managed secrets, identity/login and HTTPS. Developer can expand a selected capability **in place** to see provider preference:
  - `Automatic (recommended)` is selected by default.
  - Optional explicit choice lists actual *compatible* providers/instances for the active Target; show proposed resolved realization and reason, not a hard-coded list.
  - No mandatory provider questionnaire or advanced page; focus stays compact, accessible, keyboard navigable and progressive.
- **One flow, two existing authorities**: wizard writes capability intent only to the existing Application Contract and optional explicit provider preference only to the existing Target/deployment/operator binding owner. No forced separate manual editing or newly invented config file; do not write `provider: postgresql` into portable application intent.
- Short preview shows selected provider (automatic/explicit), reused vs new managed dependencies/containers, incremental RAM estimate with unknown/estimated/measured label. `No` returns to checklist with capability/provider selections retained; `Yes` uses existing diff/preflight/confirm/apply/verify path; cancellation and EOF/non-TTY never silently write.
- Editing the same app later must hydrate **both** current capability selections and resolved/explicit provider preference without overriding another Target's choice.
- CLI/JSON/MCP and Console reuse #872 provider resolution semantics. Explicit provider preference must be discoverable to machine clients with typed errors and equivalent authorization/confirmation, without copying TUI logic.
- Reuse supported rich capability manifests and authoritative binding owners; no parser rewrite, parallel state registry, migration project or unconsented data destruction. Do not preserve obsolete developer-authored IDs as compatibility scope.

Acceptance:
- [ ] No app ID prompt and minimal authored YAML.
- [ ] SQL capability can remain Automatic or choose a compatible available specific provider from one wizard.
- [ ] Same app intent deploys against two Targets with different explicit provider instances without altering portable YAML.
- [ ] Wizard back-loop retains both levels of selection; no hidden writes.
- [ ] Missing/ambiguous/incompatible provider handled safely with concrete next action.


## Provider-removal UX requirement (2026-10-11)

Consume #872's binding provider-removal impact/continuity result. Before confirmation show the affected apps, lost secret-management/PKI/login functions, actual certificate/token renewal consequences, secure continuation/replacement, retained data and blocked prerequisites. No generic confirmation or silent unauthenticated/plaintext fallback. Preserve choices on return; cancellation never mutates. Implement no separate impact engine in the UI.


## Universal provider-impact UX clarification (2026-10-11)

The requirement applies to ALL supported providers, not just OpenBao/Identity. Consume #872's universal typed consequence plan: affected apps/functions/dependencies, before/after provider realization and access, retained/transferred/deleted data and actual locations, operational/security consequences, prerequisites and blockers. Show actual final dispositions after execution and partial failure. No generic provider warning list, secret disclosure, invented destination or UI-local impact engine. Stop, removal, replacement and capability disable have distinct effects.


## Binding needs-first wizard UX (2026-10-11)

The wizard asks what the application/developer NEEDS, not which infrastructure product to install. Do not ask “Do you need OpenBao?”, “Install Keycloak?” or equivalent provider-brand questions in the default flow. Present a compact editable needs checklist in plain developer language, for example:
- “Do you need securely managed secrets/passwords?”
- “Do you need TLS/HTTPS for your application?”
- “Do users need to sign in to your application?”
- “Do you need persistent relational data?”
- “Do you need a cache?”
These illustrate wording, not an exhaustive capability catalog or mandatory sequential questionnaire. Use concise contextual explanations and disclose additional needs progressively.

Distinguish application user authentication from BaseHarbor operator/team access and provider service accounts. “Users” must not silently enable all three. TLS must not implicitly request Identity, OpenBao or a full Core; secure secret management does not implicitly request PKI or dynamic credentials. Genuine dependencies come from the accepted #872 resolver and are explained in the preview, without requiring the developer to choose them individually.

Translate these needs into the existing capability intent and resolve suitable providers automatically against the selected Target. Display the actual realization and required dependencies transparently in the preview (“managed secrets -> OpenBao”, where actually resolved), including reuse/new resources and concrete effects. Provider names are implementation information in the preview and optional in-place advanced preferences, not prerequisite knowledge or required questions. Existing explicit compatible-provider choice remains available without leaving this flow.

Creating and editing use the same needs vocabulary and retain choices on back-navigation. Zero selected needs remains valid. Changes consume #872's full shared consequences/required-action model and confirmations; no new resolver, invented capabilities or storage owner. This clarification governs the wording and behavior of all earlier checklist/provider-choice sections.

Additional acceptance:
- [ ] A developer can create/edit an app with protected secrets, TLS and/or user login without knowing any provider product names.
- [ ] User login, operator access and service credentials are not conflated; TLS/secrets do not silently enable unrelated capabilities.
- [ ] Preview explains the actual selected providers and genuine dependencies; optional explicit preference remains accessible in place.
